Params: Many Years Ago\nDomain Training Grounds, F.O.S. Starship, Babylonia
To ensure a comprehensive education, the academy supplemented its extensive holographic simulation pods with live-fire training sites, where projections met real ammunition.
The blast door to Range 004 slid open without a sound before you. At the center stood a single red figure, hands clasped behind her back.
Unmoved by your arrival, she lifted her right arm. Its segmented armor shifted and locked, transforming into a gun barrel that caught the harsh overhead light.
The words barely left her mouth. Holographic projections blazed to life. Virtual drones swarmed overhead, their barrage sweeping down upon the Construct in a torrent of light and sound.

She went to ground immediately, tumbling through rapid rolls before sliding into cover. She took a beat to steady herself, then rose just enough to fire from a horizontal reclined angle. The crash of the destroyed drone had barely sounded when she was already on her feet, racing toward the first firing position.

The exercise was a timed positional seizure drill, with firing points placed at uneven intervals before the targets. Each position varied in sight alignment, available rests, and tactical cover, each offering a distinct set of challenges. To pass, one only needed to score effectively from half of them.
The female Construct, however, never stopped to weigh her options. She moved, aimed, and fired in a single unbroken motion, devoid of doubt or delay.
The timer stopped the moment the last target flared with sparks. The total elapsed time, along with every individual position split, settled on numbers that seemed impossible.
Seizing position, the key word is "seize." You need to beat the clock and the enemy.
There's no textbook answer in a real firefight. Intel gets you as far as the deployment phase. After that, you trust your gut.
She folded the arm gun back into place and rested her palm on her shoulder. The residual heat from the volley radiated through the plating.
Field training exists to forge that gut feeling, and the nerve to follow it. I read your sim logs. You've got the instinct. Trust it.

The maverick "devil instructor" acknowledged you with a curt nod. You had no solid reason to claim such understanding, and yet her face, though rarely expressive, always seemed legible to you. And sometimes, in a fleeting moment of distraction, a strange feeling would creep in. Her face felt familiar, but her frame was that of a stranger.
Today's the one day off you've had in weeks. Even the grinders have gone home. And yet here you are, staring off into space. What, planning to stick around and practice with me all day?
Her red eyes, etched with the concentric circles of a sniper's sight, fixed on you. Their gaze was calm and steady.
You've got something weighing on you. Something you don't want in the logs, and you'd rather your fellow cadets not hear.
I've killed the surveillance. Out with it.
You set aside the nagging doubts and retrieved a specific simulation test from your terminal, projecting the miniaturized battlefield before you.
All prior combat data sat alongside it. Every attempt logged since the test went live, and every single one had ended in failure.
Adelyde, however, did not so much as glance at the projection. She waited in silence for you to continue.
Instructor, I've gone through all the test records, not just mine, but every cadet's.
This was designed to be impossible to win, wasn't it?
Is that getting under your skin?
Adelyde offered no denial. Her reaction spoke volumes, validating the daring suspicion that had taken root in your mind.
Like you just told me, instructor. I'm trusting my instincts.
What if I told you it really is a no-way-out situation?
The Construct instructor let out a quiet sigh, and her gaze softened along with it.
Believing in victory and staring down defeat, two sides of the same coin.
The purpose of this test is to let you feel the fear of death and learn to carry it.
To lead your squad with a clear head even when that fear grips you, that's a non-negotiable trait for every Task Force commandant.
You're the first cadet to come straight to me with this. If you're not convinced, you must have something else in mind.
Every F.O.S. simulation is modeled after a real combat engagement.
But the source record for this one... I couldn't find it anywhere in the archives.
I want to find out who left that record behind, what they chose, and how it ended for them.
You waved the simulation larger. A towering metal structure, collapsing in silence, hung between you. From afar, it looked like a bloodshot eye.
Adelyde walked forward, stepped into the giant pupil, and let the data pass right through her.
And then, I'll fight for a way out, together with that person.
<size=40>Did you ever see light reaching through the abyss, sky and ocean dreaming as one, and the world full of songs and wonders?</size>
<size=40>Did you ever see light piercing the water, sky and ocean burning as one, and the world left with nothing but red and me?</size>
<size=40>Who dared to swim against the current of time and hold me fast in my unbending will?</size>
<size=40>The souls of the Atlantic sleep on.</size>
<size=40>Its children stand watch through the endless night.</size>
Shortly After the Second Atlantic Calamity
Shortly After the Second Atlantic Calamity\nChief of Staff's Office, General Staff, Babylonia
Wells! Cutting side deals with them behind my back, is that what I gave you intelligence priority and full analytic access for?
You think having enemies at our door means I've got my hands tied? The second this goes sideways, your head's on the block!
The man storms through the door, anger barely leashed. Outside, a wrinkled face greets him, every fold stretched into a knowing smirk.
Aww, little Nicky, all done already? I was just starting to enjoy myself.
You don't see the military tearing itself apart every day. Can you really blame me for staying to watch the show?
The Chief Commander's voice drops to a flat, measured calm. Whatever fire seething inside him never reaches the surface; it hardens into ice and is quickly tucked away.
He pushes aside the Kurono executive in his way and strides out, deaf to the protest trailing behind him.

The silver-haired man enters with a rueful shake of his head. He acknowledges the rigid chair by the desk with a passing glance, then drifts to the sofa, settling into its cushions at a lazy angle, every bit the master of the space.
Across the room, Wells pulls off his glasses and wipes them clean. The shadows under his eyes tell a story of sleepless nights.
I don't recall your name on my calendar today.
Cold. Real cold, when I came all this way to save your skin.
Don't worry, little Nicky's got his hands full. Between that moon rock strike and the gaping wound in the "mega water pump," he's not gonna have time to breathe down your neck.
He won't—no, wouldn't dare—block your little off-the-books relief gig. And once that's wrapped up...
The man dragged out his syllables with clear purpose, then spread his hands toward the person behind the desk.
Well, let's just say the military's chain of command might look a little different by then.
With his coat hanging loose over his shoulders, the Chief of Staff presses two fingers to his brow and chooses to ignore the loaded words entirely.
The only reason you'd show up in person is if there's real progress on the deal, and you're already sure of it.
A way past the Atlantic Eye's inner and outer perimeters, the full blueprints, or the Watcher Society members? Go ahead. How much can you squeeze out of the TEC?

As the Atlantic Red Tide crisis deepens and humanity's forces press steadily toward its epicenter, the Atlantic Eye, three unresolved concerns weigh on every commander both at the front and behind the lines.

First, access to the Atlantic Eye. After the Atlantic Calamity, the Ananke system has sealed the dam from within, and the rogue Comet Patrol Array has choked the skies and waters outside. So, how do we get in?
Second, navigation itself. Assuming a way in can be found, where are the interior maps?

Third, since the Atlantic Calamity, a handful of survivors have founded the Watcher Society. Identified as core personnel by the Transatlantic Economic Community, they and their students have been restricted from leaving the region. For years, they have kept an exceptionally low profile.
The three tactical resources the Chief of Staff has just laid out are precisely the very reason why negotiations between Babylonia and the Transatlantic Economic Community have hit a wall.
The resources Babylonia is requesting go to the very core of our technological lifeblood. Our terms are premised on equity. We want full access to the Omega File.
Wider distribution of Omega Weapons serves the unified front against the Punishing Virus that your side has championed. More hands, more strength.
Yet even during the Balder's construction at Port Podesta, you barred our researchers from direct contact with the Omega Device, let alone accessing the Omega File itself.
I must be frank: we have not seen a corresponding measure of good faith from your side in this arrangement.
You speak of good faith. We speak of duty.

The origin and ground zero of this crisis both fall under the Transatlantic Economic Community's purview. You are obligated to share intelligence, not to dismiss our humanitarian effort as some sort of business transaction.
Then are you prepared to take responsibility for the kinetic strike launched from the lunar surface?
For heaven's sake! Our soldiers and your people are out there fighting their way through the Red Tide as we speak, and you're using this time to trade accusations?!
That's enough. Recess, twenty minutes. You, with me.
Nikola's not seeing the bigger picture. Kurono can accomplish much more than all of you can in another two weeks of table-pounding.

We know how to make those families see reason, and we're not exactly strangers to each other. If you want us as your go-between, Chief of Staff, you can't expect results without putting something on the table yourself.
Simple: one down payment, two final fees.
The down payment's already cleared. The Construct who spearheaded the Atlantic Calamity rescue, Adelyde, now an F.O.S. instructor, is heading to the Atlantic Eye with our "gracious company."
As for the final fees... from this point on, any Kurono team we deploy to the Atlantic Eye answers to no military authority.
And whatever tech assets our team pulls out of that dam, they belong to Kurono, and Kurono alone.
The eyes behind the glasses carry no warmth as they turn toward him. When the Chief of Staff of Babylonia finally speaks, her voice comes out low and measured.
What's the problem? You don't trust your own Task Force? Or maybe not even your Gray Raven Commandant?
Without the Science Council's support, whatever you recover will be useless to you.
Anyone with half a brain can see it. The Sefirot are the cornerstone of the next era. You're in the thick of it with that "disciple" and expecting us to just stand by? Not happening.
Wells' hand clamps down on his own wrist.
The silver-haired man sees it as a game, and humanity has no choice but to play for the win.
But the key to that victory lies firmly coiled in the serpent's grasp on the opposite side of the table.
The probability of success falls with each passing second. Can he really allow that serpent to loosen its hold on the key, only to slither toward the world's very lifeline?
He pushes himself up from the desk, forcing his stiff spine to straighten, and reaches out his hand to the serpent.
A flicker of surprise crosses Collins' eyes. He hesitates for a beat, then lets out a booming laugh as he rises from the sofa.
Haha... Hahaha! Now that's the spirit!
I had you pegged as the same old academic, always overthinking, too proud for your own good. Guess no one really knows their limits until they hit the wall.
He closes the distance in a few easy strides and takes the Chief of Staff's hand, giving it a firm, deliberate shake.

Credit goes to your Engineering Force's Karenina and 【kuroname】, who came through as always. Now that the Atlantic comms are back up, those talents the TEC's been keeping under wraps will be en route to the front line this week.

The blueprints will arrive with them. The Comet Patrol Array was their creation, mind you. Just put them in a position where they've got no other choice, and pray these people know how to undo the cage they built.
The man in black-rimmed glasses withdraws his hand before his composure slips.
You're sending them in as mine-sniffing rats.
Don't be dramatic. Issuing orders is literally in the Chief of Staff's job description.
If you want Kurono to take the blame instead, be my guest. But then I'll be taking that chair of yours, because clearly you're done with it.
Collins taps the table lightly. When he speaks again, his voice takes on a sharper edge.
The real headache is Ananke. From what we've gathered, it seems that it can emit a ray that bends local spacetime, freezing the dam in the moment right before the calamity hit.
And looking at what the Atlantic's become, I'd say Ananke is in pretty rough shape. It's something Dominik built behind Erhorn's back, and not a soul has set eyes on it since the Atlantic Calamity.
No one setting eyes on it after doesn't mean no one set eyes on it then. I know exactly why you made sure Adelyde was on your list, Collins.
Just then, a buzz cuts through the room from Collins' terminal. He glances at the caller ID and holds the device up with a grin.
Well, well, speak of the devil. It's the transatlantic ship the instructor's on. One of ours. Mind if I take this here?
The call goes through with a beep.
Backup for what?! Where's Clausen? Get him on the line!
The captain's been put down and tied up. I barely got clear. It's Adelyde—
The feed shifts to reveal a shadowy ship interior. The terminal delivers every sound from the other end back into the office with startling clarity.
Quiet settles in. Then a steady tap of combat heels against metal deck grows closer, then comes to a halt.
The door bursts open with a deafening crack. Collins barely registers a streak of red before it is upon the crew member.
The feed jerks upward. A massive cross cannon slams into the wall beside the Kurono crew member's head with a heavy thud.
I'll talk! Anything! Just get that thing away from me!!
All I've done for three years is follow orders... and maybe grab free food from the World Government's cafeteria while my cover ID's still valid. That's it! I swear... I never did any real damage!
Give me the terminal. I didn't ask about your lunch habits.
The white-haired Construct takes the terminal and holds it up.
I won't be needing it anymore.
Adelyde looks away, a frown touching her features at the sight of the crew members sprawling on the floor.
I only put down the ones who kept trying to block me. They'd better recover quickly. The Atlantic Eye needs every capable pair of hands it can get.
Your soldiers could use more drilling.
She ends the call without another word.
Ahem... it seems Adelyde has her own interpretation of "escort."
When she's set on something, even I don't get a say.
Collins' face twitches. He forced the smile back into place, his jaw tight.
At least she's still bound for the Atlantic Eye. You got your end of the bargain. Our deal holds.
Of course. I'm not petty enough to torch a deal over one uppity firecracker.
The Kurono executive seems to have finally lost interest. He turns to leave, but his steps halt before the standing cabinet by the wall.
With his back to Wells, he raises a hand and taps a precise spot on the glass door.
Your act of burying the hatchet could use some work. You can't even bring yourself to put this away.
Nurturing a partnership takes time and energy. You want to be the virtuous one; fine by me. Just don't let your past drag you down and leave this pretend businessman holding the bag.
Only when the last footstep fades does Wells step out from behind the desk. He walks to the cabinet and retrieves the object Collins pointed at.
It's a well-maintained sidearm, standard issue for the Babylonia Task Force. A small silver falcon emblem is engraved along the barrel.
His thumb traces the bird's outstretched wings.
The Chief of Staff closes his fingers over the gun's mounting base. The mechanism reads his palm and parts silently, exposing a terminal nestled inside.
The screen glows to life. On it sits a single mission interface, one that has already pushed past a critical milestone.
There's no turning back from here on.
Well, let's see how far this narrow gray path will carry me...
